findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; recorded affinities were removed and an equal score prior applies, so no observed affinity label is available to either role.

The observed window is the score-time grid 0.0-0.49 with learning window [0.0,0.5]; all continuous contrast fits are restricted to observed nodes with extrapolation disallowed, so no time-conditioned rule may be evaluated outside this support.

Continuous landmark contrast features show sign changes and strong sign conflicts across the observed window (e.g. landmark_00_local_dy has 6 sign changes and 4 strong conflicts; landmark_00_local_cxy has 9 sign changes and 14 strong conflicts), and no polynomial fit is accepted, so a constant rule is not supported over a time-conditioned rule for these coordinates.

First-to-last rate reversals are large for several landmark coordinates (e.g. landmark_00_local_dy first_rate_z -72.4 versus last_rate_z +5.5; landmark_00_local_cxy +64.8 versus -19.7), indicating the direction of change is not stable across the observed window.

Whole-window z values for the read landmark features are small relative to their first/last rate z values (e.g. landmark_00_soft_mass whole_window_z 0.64 with first_rate_z 9.27 and last_rate_z -10.00), so endpoint-rate evidence and whole-window mean evidence are not interchangeable summaries.

hypotheses.direction: time-conditioned rather than constant contrast weighting
hypotheses.falsifier: a constant rule matching the observed-node contrast signs and rates within the reported node RMSE
hypotheses.observable: sign and rate of the landmark contrast features at observed score nodes
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned contrast rule over observed score nodes may better express the landmark coordinate contrasts than a constant rule, because the read features show multiple sign changes and no accepted polynomial fit within the observed window.

hypotheses.direction: descriptive only until a registered reward recipe is bound
hypotheses.falsifier: consistent same-sign first and last rates with no strong sign conflicts for the targeted coordinate
hypotheses.observable: first_rate_z versus last_rate_z sign agreement for the targeted coordinate
hypotheses.scope: observed selection nodes and complete observed window
hypotheses.statement: Landmark local displacement and cross-term coordinates carry unstable direction information, so a coordinate intervention targeting them should be tested against a discriminating failure condition rather than assumed favorable.

limitations: No decoded terminal labels or current-study outcome data were supplied, so last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

Only continuous_trends rows were read; branch_adjusted, endpoint_effects, increment_effects, joint_diagnostics, regional_effects, survival_effects and turnover_accounting were not inspected, so multiplicity-adjusted ranking, joint coupling and turnover accounting questions remain unanswered.
No absolute geometric or physical interaction-energy claim is made; the read features are untyped coordinate proxies in predicted endpoint world coordinates.
No temperature edit is proposed or evaluated; temperatures are immutable task parameters.
